faq.a: Ahmad is associated with the Arabic form أحمد, whose core sense is most praiseworthy, most commendable.

faq.q: What is the origin of Ahmad?
faq.a: Ahmad is associated with Arabic. Aḥmad ('most praiseworthy'), elative of حامد; the Prophet's name. The source record left this name with no origin and no script form.
Yes — the underlying form أحمد is Arabic.
Ahmad can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Ahmad should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. أحمد occurs in the Qur'an (Sūrat al-Ṣaff 61:6) as a name of the Prophet

faq.a: Romanization variants include Ahmad, ahmad. Script forms are أحمد, احمد, अहमद.
